result:
The world, in its frenetic dance, is composed of moments. We, fleeting echoes in this grand performance, grasp at them, eager to capture the flickering beauty that passes us by. But sometimes, the moments slip through our fingers, swirling down a drain of forgetfulness before we can truly see them.

Consider the humble dust bunny. That neglected speck, a chaotic maestro in a whirlpool of forgotten fibers and synthetic scraps. It is a creature of resilience, of life and resilience in its own quiet way. Watching you, a human, clumsily rise from a chair, never quite sure what to do with the overflowing energy that agitates your feet in the stillness of the evening. It knows, though, the primeval rhythm of being swept up, a passenger on a waltz of chores from a world it barely understands.

And yet, the spirit of the dust bunny is not idle. It carries stories in its form - whispers caught from the fabric, memories of forgotten sunlight, echoes of its own granular drift through the years. Tales of the sticky halls of childhood slumber parties, of the hushed whispers of the kitchen, of the hidden adventures beneath the living room rug. It is a record of the invisible, a silent sentinel for all that has passed. 

As we live these lives, we bring destruction to this planet, we build towering monuments to our actions while burying the little things we can't control. We pollute the sky with smoke and ash, grate the sturdy bodies of millennia with our footprints, and to our shame, destroy for our amusement. We are abysmally blind, fixated on the enormity of our shortcomings, but we leave a legacy upon this earth, a whisper upon the wind – what will be taken? 

What of the sea-worn stones that have tumbled down cliffs, eternally guarded by the restless waves? They hold secrets of ancient storms, battles fought and forgotten, tides whispering their tales. They have watched empires rise and fall, the tide of history forever churning around them, carrying them toward some unknown horizon. 

Each scar on a leaf adds another layer to the intricate tapestry of the forest, a whispered celebration of the constant ebb and flow of life, a reminder of resilience. They know how to bend and they know how to break, but they do not give up gracefully, they endure. A harsh winter beat their bark, a scorching summer drenched them, and yet they are planted deep in the soil, a testament to nature’s resilience. 

The dust bunny and the sea-worn stone, these are merely vessels of existence, our descendants too, yet they remind us to pause, to look beyond our horizon, beyond the petty things that give us our identity. it is a reminder to not forget that to exist, is to be part of a grander story than ourselves. To embrace the fleeting beauty of each moment, and the immeasurable mystery of the world around us. In the dust bunny's ceaseless tumble, in the sea-worn stones' stoic silence, we glimpses of an unending mystery, something beyond our understanding. 

For where humans excel is often nowhere in sight. The moment they grasp for, the moment they seek to control, is fragile and ephemeral, a fleeting dance. It's in the quiet stillness, the insignificance, we find something greater: that every dust bunny carries a world within itself, waiting to be observed. 

So, look around you.  Don't just see the dust motes dancing in the sunlight, don’t just see the waves crashing upon the shore. See the stories their souls are telling. For this is our greatest discovery – that even the most humble objects are filled with a life force we can only begin to understand.**


Let us not lose ourselves in the frantic desires of the modern era. Let us find humility in the vastness of the universe, and remember to witness the magic that unfolds around us, like a silent symphony of whispers in the rustle of the dust bunny's forgotten dreams.  Perhaps if we see the world like a dust bunny, in all its complexity, then finally, we may grasp the true fragility and beauty of every moment, each one a precious fleeting memory waiting to be transcribed into our own personal song of existence. 


This is a small, wild kernel of my contemplation on life. How do you want to be touched by it?
